records.label: spacr.chaining#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: :mod:`spacr.ports` now declares what each module consumes and produces, and :mod:`spacr.artifacts` records where every finished run put its outputs.  This module joins the two:
records.translation: :mod:`spacr.ports` अब घोषित करता है कि प्रत्येक मॉड्यूल क्या ग्रहण करता है और क्या उत्पन्न करता है, और :mod:`spacr.artifacts` दर्ज करता है कि हर पूर्ण निष्पादन ने अपने आउटपुट कहाँ रखे।  यह मॉड्यूल इन दोनों को जोड़ता है:

records.context: :func:`chained_inputs` asks the registry — ``latest(kind, project=…)`` — where the upstream module's output *is*, and turns that into the value a setting name should hold.  The answer comes from the row the producer wrote, not from re-deriving ``<root>/merged``;
records.label: spacr.chaining#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: :func:`chained_inputs` asks the registry — ``latest(kind, project=…)`` — where the upstream module's output *is*, and turns that into the value a settings key should hold.  The answer comes from the row the producer wrote, not from re-deriving ``<root>/merged``;
records.translation: :func:`chained_inputs` रजिस्ट्री से पूछता है — ``latest(kind, project=…)`` — कि अपस्ट्रीम मॉड्यूल का आउटपुट *वास्तव में* कहाँ है, और उसे उस मान में बदलता है जो किसी सेटिंग कुंजी में होना चाहिए।  उत्तर उस पंक्ति से आता है जिसे उत्पादक ने लिखा था, न कि ``<root>/merged`` को दोबारा व्युत्पन्न करने से;

records.context: :func:`resolve_settings` applies those values to a settings key-value mapping **without ever overwriting a path the user edited**.  A user edit is remembered in a :class:`PinStore` and takes precedence until it is cleared; when the upstream later moves, the new location is *offered* (:class:`HeldPin`) rather than pushed;
records.label: spacr.chaining#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: :func:`resolve_settings` applies those values to a settings dict **without ever overwriting a path the user edited**.  A user edit is remembered in a :class:`PinStore` and takes precedence until it is cleared; when the upstream later moves, the new location is *offered* (:class:`HeldPin`) rather than pushed;
records.translation: :func:`resolve_settings` इन मानों को किसी सेटिंग्स डिक्ट पर लागू करता है, **उपयोगकर्ता द्वारा संपादित किसी पथ को कभी अधिलेखित किए बिना**।  उपयोगकर्ता का संपादन एक :class:`PinStore` में याद रखा जाता है और हटाए जाने तक प्राथमिकता रखता है; जब बाद में अपस्ट्रीम स्थानांतरित होता है, तो नया स्थान थोपा नहीं जाता बल्कि *प्रस्तावित* किया जाता है (:class:`HeldPin`);

records.context: :func:`staleness_notes` turns :meth:`spacr.artifacts.Registry.is_stale` into sentences a user can act on, keyed by the cause codes so the reason is specific — "Mask ran again after this" is a different problem from "the settings changed";
records.label: spacr.chaining#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: :func:`staleness_notes` turns :meth:`spacr.artifacts.Registry.is_stale` into sentences a user can act on, keyed by the cause codes so the reason is specific — "Mask ran again after this" is a different problem from "the settings changed";
records.translation: :func:`staleness_notes` :meth:`spacr.artifacts.Registry.is_stale` को ऐसे वाक्यों में बदलता है जिन पर उपयोगकर्ता कार्रवाई कर सके; ये कारण कोड के अनुसार कुंजीबद्ध होते हैं ताकि कारण विशिष्ट रहे — "Mask ran again after this" एक अलग समस्या है और "the settings changed" अलग;

records.context: :func:`next_steps` lists the modules that can execute on a finished processing session's outputs, using :func:`spacr.ports.next_modules` for the candidates, :func:`chained_inputs` for their pre-filled settings and :func:`spacr.ports.check_ready` so a successor that *cannot* run is offered with its blocking reason.
records.label: spacr.chaining#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: :func:`next_steps` lists the modules that can run on a finished run's outputs, using :func:`spacr.ports.next_modules` for the candidates, :func:`chained_inputs` for their pre-filled settings and :func:`spacr.ports.check_ready` so a successor that *cannot* run is offered with its blocking reason.
records.translation: :func:`next_steps` उन मॉड्यूलों को सूचीबद्ध करता है जो किसी पूर्ण निष्पादन के आउटपुट पर चल सकते हैं; उम्मीदवारों के लिए :func:`spacr.ports.next_modules`, उनकी पहले से भरी सेटिंग्स के लिए :func:`chained_inputs` और :func:`spacr.ports.check_ready` का उपयोग होता है, ताकि जो उत्तरवर्ती मॉड्यूल *नहीं* चल सकता उसे उसके अवरोधक कारण के साथ प्रस्तुत किया जाए।

records.context: **Every download is atomic, and never overwrites.** Bytes stream into a temporary file *in the destination directory* (so the final ``os.replace`` is a same-filesystem rename, which is atomic) and the rename happens only after the checksum passes. An interrupted or cancelled download therefore leaves nothing behind that looks like a model — the failure mode where half a checkpoint sits at the real filename, loads, and segments badly, cannot happen.

records.context: **Benchmarks are only comparable inside one field set.** A model's score on your three fields does not predict its score on somebody else's, and a table that sorts the two together produces a ranking of two unrelated numbers. So every :class:`BenchmarkResult` records a :func:`fieldset_id` — a hash of the actual pixels, not the folder name — and :func:`rank` **raises** :class:`IncomparableBenchmarks` when handed results from more than one field set. :func:`rank_groups` and :func:`format_benchmarks` are the supported alternative: they group by field set, rank within each group, and label the groups.

records.source: **Benchmarks are only comparable inside one field set.** A model's score on your three fields does not predict its score on somebody else's, and a table that sorts the two together produces a ranking of two unrelated numbers. So every :class:`BenchmarkResult` records a :func:`fieldset_id` — a hash of the actual pixels, not the folder name — and :func:`rank` **raises** :class:`IncomparableBenchmarks` when handed results from more than one field set. :func:`rank_groups` and :func:`format_benchmarks` are the supported alternative: they group by field set, rank within each group, and label the groups.
records.translation: **बेंचमार्क केवल एक छवि क्षेत्र समूह के भीतर तुलनीय हैं।** आपके तीन छवि क्षेत्रों पर किसी मॉडल का स्कोर किसी और के छवि क्षेत्रों पर उसके स्कोर का पूर्वानुमान नहीं देता, और जो तालिका दोनों को एक साथ क्रमबद्ध करती है वह दो असंबंधित संख्याओं की श्रेणी बनाती है। इसलिए हर :class:`BenchmarkResult` एक :func:`fieldset_id` दर्ज करता है — वास्तविक पिक्सेलों का हैश, फ़ोल्डर नाम का नहीं — और :func:`rank` एक से अधिक छवि क्षेत्र समूहों के परिणाम मिलने पर **त्रुटि उठाता है**, अर्थात :class:`IncomparableBenchmarks`। :func:`rank_groups` और :func:`format_benchmarks` समर्थित विकल्प हैं: वे छवि क्षेत्र समूह के अनुसार समूहित करते हैं, प्रत्येक समूह के भीतर श्रेणी देते हैं, और समूहों को लेबल करते हैं।

records.context: There is no ground truth here. :func:`benchmark` runs one model over N microscope fields of view and reports what came out: object counts, timings and the :mod:`spacr.seg_qc` verdict per microscope field of view (fused? shattered? empty? all on the border?). That is a *quality-control* score, not an accuracy — it can tell you a model collapsed on your data, it cannot tell you which of two plausible segmentations is right. :data:`RANK_KEYS` therefore offers exactly two structured-data names, ``'qc'`` and ``'seconds'``, and no structured-data name that would read as accuracy. To compare two models against each other, use :func:`compare_entries`, which hands both to :func:`spacr.model_compare.compare_models` — the A/B harness that is explicit about neither side being the truth.

records.context: **Every download is checksummed, and verification happens before use.** A checkpoint truncated by a dropped connection, or swapped for a different one at the same URL, still loads. It does not throw; it produces silently different masks, and the run that used it looks exactly like the run that did not. So :func:`fetch` hashes what arrived and compares it to the hash the catalogue published: a mismatch deletes the file and throws :class:`ChecksumMismatch` — the entry is never registered. The hash that was actually computed is stored on the returned entry, so "verified" means "these bytes", not "this filename".

records.context: The rules, in order:
records.label: spacr.model_zoo.classify_kind#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The rules, in order:
records.translation: नियम, क्रम में:

records.context: 1. ``*.CP_model`` is a Cellpose checkpoint — that is what :func:`spacr.submodules.train_cellpose` names its output. 2. ``*.pth`` / ``*.pt`` is a machine-learning classification model checkpoint (:func:`spacr.io._save_model` writes ``<model_type>_epoch_<n>_channels_<ch>.pth``) **unless** it sits in a Cellpose folder or has ``cellpose``/``cp_model`` in its name. 3. An **extensionless** file inside a Cellpose folder is a Cellpose checkpoint only if its first bytes are a torch save. ``cellpose.train`` writes ``<save_path>/models/<name>`` with no suffix, and that folder also holds READMEs and logs — the magic-byte check is what keeps a ``README`` out of the zoo. 4. Anything else is not a model. CSVs, PNGs, ``.npy`` masks and settings snapshots all land here and are ignored.
records.label: spacr.model_zoo.classify_kind#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. ``*.CP_model`` is a Cellpose checkpoint — that is what :func:`spacr.submodules.train_cellpose` names its output. 2. ``*.pth`` / ``*.pt`` is a classifier checkpoint (:func:`spacr.io._save_model` writes ``<model_type>_epoch_<n>_channels_<ch>.pth``) **unless** it sits in a Cellpose folder or has ``cellpose``/``cp_model`` in its name. 3. An **extensionless** file inside a Cellpose folder is a Cellpose checkpoint only if its first bytes are a torch save. ``cellpose.train`` writes ``<save_path>/models/<name>`` with no suffix, and that folder also holds READMEs and logs — the magic-byte check is what keeps a ``README`` out of the zoo. 4. Anything else is not a model. CSVs, PNGs, ``.npy`` masks and settings snapshots all land here and are ignored.
records.translation: 1. ``*.CP_model`` एक Cellpose चेकपॉइंट है — :func:`spacr.submodules.train_cellpose` अपने आउटपुट को यही नाम देता है। 2. ``*.pth`` / ``*.pt`` एक क्लासिफ़ायर चेकपॉइंट है (:func:`spacr.io._save_model` ``<model_type>_epoch_<n>_channels_<ch>.pth`` लिखता है) **जब तक कि** वह किसी Cellpose फ़ोल्डर में न हो या उसके नाम में ``cellpose``/``cp_model`` न हो। 3. Cellpose फ़ोल्डर के भीतर **बिना एक्सटेंशन वाली** फ़ाइल केवल तभी Cellpose चेकपॉइंट है जब उसके पहले बाइट्स torch सेव हों। ``cellpose.train`` बिना प्रत्यय के ``<save_path>/models/<name>`` लिखता है, और उस फ़ोल्डर में READMEs और लॉग भी होते हैं — मैजिक-बाइट जाँच ही ``README`` को मॉडल संग्रह से बाहर रखती है। 4. बाकी कुछ भी मॉडल नहीं है। CSVs, PNGs, ``.npy`` मास्क और सेटिंग्स स्नैपशॉट सब यहीं आते हैं और अनदेखे किए जाते हैं।

records.context: The post-processing of empanada's Panoptic-DeepLab models, ported so spaCR does not depend on empanada-dl. A pixel is mitochondrion when ``semantic`` reaches ``threshold``. Instance centres are the local maxima of ``centres`` in a ``centre_window`` square that reach ``centre_threshold``. Each mitochondrion pixel votes, through its ``offsets`` (row, column), for the place its centre is, and joins the nearest centre found. Instances smaller than ``min_size`` pixels are dropped and the rest are numbered 1..n in raster order of their centres.
records.label: spacr.model_zoo.mitonet_instances#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The post-processing of empanada's Panoptic-DeepLab models, ported so spaCR does not depend on empanada-dl. A pixel is mitochondrion when ``semantic`` reaches ``threshold``. Instance centres are the local maxima of ``centres`` in a ``centre_window`` square that reach ``centre_threshold``. Each mitochondrion pixel votes, through its ``offsets`` (row, column), for the place its centre is, and joins the nearest centre found. Instances smaller than ``min_size`` pixels are dropped and the rest are numbered 1..n in raster order of their centres.
records.translation: empanada के Panoptic-DeepLab मॉडलों का पश्च-प्रसंस्करण, जिसे यहाँ लाया गया है ताकि spaCR empanada-dl पर निर्भर न रहे। कोई पिक्सेल माइटोकॉन्ड्रियन है जब ``semantic`` ``threshold`` तक पहुँचता है। उदाहरण केंद्र ``centres`` के वे स्थानीय अधिकतम हैं, एक ``centre_window`` वर्ग में, जो ``centre_threshold`` तक पहुँचते हैं। प्रत्येक माइटोकॉन्ड्रियन पिक्सेल अपने ``offsets`` (पंक्ति, स्तंभ) के माध्यम से उस स्थान के लिए मत देता है जहाँ उसका केंद्र है, और निकटतम पाए गए केंद्र से जुड़ता है। ``min_size`` पिक्सेल से छोटे उदाहरण हटा दिए जाते हैं और बाकी को उनके केंद्रों के रास्टर क्रम में 1..n क्रमांक दिए जाते हैं।

records.context: It does not fetch on Qt's main GUI execution path. This function is reached from ``spacr.settings.downloaded_zoo_models`` while a settings panel is being built, so it ran inside ``MainWindow._on_nav_selected`` with nothing able to paint or answer the compositor. Measured with the catalogue host non-routable (10.255.255.1, the shape of a down VPN or a captive portal -- the connect neither completes nor is refused): opening the Mask module took **32.2 s**, all of it a main GUI execution path stuck in ``urlopen``. GNOME asks a window whether it is alive after five seconds, so the user saw GNOME's "force quit" dialog. With the fetch moved off the independent execution path the same open took 2.4 s.

records.translation: यह Qt के GUI थ्रेड पर प्राप्ति नहीं करता। यह फ़ंक्शन ``spacr.settings.downloaded_zoo_models`` से तब पहुँचा जाता है जब कोई सेटिंग्स पैनल बन रहा होता है, इसलिए यह ``MainWindow._on_nav_selected`` के भीतर चलता था, जब कुछ भी चित्रित नहीं कर सकता था या कंपोज़िटर को उत्तर नहीं दे सकता था। कैटलॉग होस्ट को अमार्गणीय रखकर मापा गया (10.255.255.1, जो बंद VPN या कैप्टिव पोर्टल जैसी स्थिति है -- कनेक्शन न पूरा होता है न अस्वीकृत): Mask मॉड्यूल खोलने में **32.2 s** लगे, सारा समय GUI थ्रेड ``urlopen`` में अटका रहा। GNOME पाँच सेकंड बाद किसी विंडो से पूछता है कि क्या वह जीवित है, इसलिए उपयोगकर्ता ने GNOME का "force quit" संवाद देखा। प्राप्ति को थ्रेड से हटाने पर वही खोलना 2.4 s में हुआ।

records.context: ``spacr.ml.regression_model`` can return a statsmodels ``OLS``, ``WLS``, ``RLM``, ``QuantReg``, a ``GLM`` in any of six families, a ``MixedLM``, a ``BetaModel``, a sklearn ``Lasso``/``Ridge``/``ElasticNet`` or a ``LinearSVC``. Those objects agree on almost nothing: a sklearn ``Lasso`` has no p-values, no covariance matrix and no ``fittedvalues``; a ``MixedLM`` has no hat matrix; a Gaussian model has no calibration curve worth drawing. Every panel therefore either draws or raises :class:`PanelUnavailable` carrying the *reason*, and the reason is printed on the combined report page and returned in the manifest. A panel is never silently omitted, and never faked with a substitute statistic that does not mean what the axis label says.
records.label: spacr.regression_qc#12
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context

records.context: Two numbers, because they answer different questions. The *unscaled* condition number is what ``statsmodels`` prints in a summary, and it is dominated by the units of the columns: a predictor measured in cells rather than thousands of cells changes it by 1000 with no change in the science. The *scaled* one (each column normalised to unit length first, the Belsley-Kuh-Welsch definition) is unit-free and is the one whose thresholds — 30, 100, 1000 — mean anything.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Two numbers, because they answer different questions. The *unscaled* condition number is what ``statsmodels`` prints in a summary, and it is dominated by the units of the columns: a predictor measured in cells rather than thousands of cells changes it by 1000 with no change in the science. The *scaled* one (each column normalised to unit length first, the Belsley-Kuh-Welsch definition) is unit-free and is the one whose thresholds — 30, 100, 1000 — mean anything.

records.translation: हर पैनल का प्रयास किया जाता है। जिस पैनल की इस मॉडल के लिए गणना नहीं हो सकती — Lasso से कोई p-मान नहीं, मेटाडेटा में कोई प्लेट स्तंभ नहीं, Gaussian फ़िट के लिए कोई अंशांकन नहीं — उसे कारण सहित ``skipped`` दर्ज किया जाता है, संयुक्त पृष्ठ पर धूसर टाइल के रूप में दिखाया जाता है और पाठ रिपोर्ट में सूचीबद्ध किया जाता है। इसे कभी चुपचाप हटाया नहीं जाता, क्योंकि "the panel is not there" और "the panel is fine" एक जैसे नहीं दिखने चाहिए।

records.context: Computed from the inverse of the predictor *correlation* matrix — the identity ``VIF_j = (R^-1)_jj`` — rather than by running ``p`` auxiliary regressions. On a screening experiment design with 1,200 gRNA columns the auxiliary- regression route is ``O(p^4)`` and is impractical; the correlation route is one ``O(p^3)`` decomposition. The two agree exactly when the design contains an intercept (see the test that pins this against ``statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence.variance_inflation_factor``).

records.source: Computed from the inverse of the predictor *correlation* matrix — the identity ``VIF_j = (R^-1)_jj`` — rather than by running ``p`` auxiliary regressions. On a screen design with 1,200 gRNA columns the auxiliary- regression route is ``O(p^4)`` and is impractical; the correlation route is one ``O(p^3)`` decomposition. records.source: Aliases are whole words. ``col`` is here because spaCR itself wrote it; a one-letter ``c`` is not, because it would capture a measurement column called ``c`` and rename a real variable into a plate key. A name that is not normalised is visible the moment a user looks at the picker; a measurement silently renamed to ``columnID`` is not, and it corrupts the join it lands in.

records.context: **A column with no values at all comes back as** ``object``. This is the common one and it is not a data problem: ``pandas.read_sql`` builds the frame from the rows it gets, so a column that is ``NULL`` in every row arrives as a column of ``None`` and pandas types that ``object`` -- even though SQLite declares it ``REAL``. spaCR writes ``NULL`` for a NaN, and whole measurements are legitimately NaN for a whole database: ``skew_intensity``/``kurtosis_intensity`` are NaN for every uniform object, and ``mode_intensity`` was NaN for every object in every database written before the SciPy shim in ``measure._extended_regionprops_table``. Such a column is converted to ``float64`` NaN, which is what it always meant. Nothing is lost, so nothing is warned about -- and the caller's own all-NaN filter then drops it and says so.

records.source: **A column with no values at all comes back as** ``object``. This is the common one and it is not a data problem: ``pandas.read_sql`` builds the frame from the rows it gets, so a column that is ``NULL`` in every row arrives as a column of ``None`` and pandas types that ``object`` -- even though SQLite declares it ``REAL``. spaCR writes ``NULL`` for a NaN, and whole measurements are legitimately NaN for a whole database: ``skew_intensity``/``kurtosis_intensity`` are NaN for every uniform object, and ``mode_intensity`` was NaN for every object in every database written before the SciPy shim in ``measure._extended_regionprops_table``. Such a column is converted to ``float64`` NaN, which is what it always meant. Nothing is lost, so nothing is warned about -- and the caller's own all-NaN filter then drops it and says so.
records.translation: **बिना किसी मान वाला स्तंभ इस रूप में लौटता है:** ``object``। यह सामान्य स्थिति है और यह डेटा की समस्या नहीं है: ``pandas.read_sql`` प्राप्त पंक्तियों से फ़्रेम बनाता है, इसलिए हर पंक्ति में ``NULL`` वाला स्तंभ ``None`` के स्तंभ के रूप में आता है और pandas उसे ``object`` प्रकार देता है -- भले ही SQLite उसे ``REAL`` घोषित करता हो। spaCR NaN के लिए ``NULL`` लिखता है, और पूरे मापन पूरे डेटाबेस के लिए वैध रूप से NaN होते हैं: ``skew_intensity``/``kurtosis_intensity`` हर एकसमान वस्तु के लिए NaN हैं, और ``mode_intensity`` ``measure._extended_regionprops_table`` में SciPy शिम से पहले लिखे गए हर डेटाबेस में हर वस्तु के लिए NaN था। ऐसा स्तंभ ``float64`` NaN में बदला जाता है, जो उसका हमेशा से अर्थ था। कुछ भी नहीं खोता, इसलिए किसी बात की चेतावनी नहीं दी जाती -- और फिर कॉलर का अपना पूर्ण-NaN फ़िल्टर उसे हटा देता है और यह बताता है।

records.context: The object prefix is stripped before the label is re-canonicalised, which is what makes this the inverse of :func:`compose_prcfo` for **every** label rather than only the numeric ones. :func:`object_id` reads an already-prefixed numeric id back out of its prefix (``'o7'`` → ``7`` → ``'o7'``), but it cannot do that for a preserved non-numeric token: without stripping, ``'oxy'`` would become ``'ooxy'`` and the key would grow on every pass through the parser.
